children: U.S. import prices ticked up in August after two months of declines, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Overall import prices rose 0.7% in August following an upwardly revised 0.3% decline in July, the data showed. A consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had been projecting a 0.4% increase for August. Year-on-year prices were up 7%, the BLS said.
Import prices exclude duties, such as tariffs imposed on imports by the Trump administration, as well as transportation costs.

Petroleum import prices edged 0.1% higher, but were more than offset on the fuel front by a 1% drop in natural gas prices. Petroleum prices had been on a downswing in recent months, but were 27% higher year-over-year in August. The price of natural gas doubled over the same period.

Prices for all nonfuel imports were up 0.8% for the month, more than offsetting the drop in fuel import prices in August, the BLS said. The increases were led by nonfuel industrial supplies and materials, capital goods and consumer goods, excluding automotives.
